learningObjective: See why a contextual-bandit log contains a reward only for the chosen action and why a target policy cannot be evaluated where the logging policy had zero support.
mediumRationale: A deterministic two-panel SVG is the smallest medium that can keep the same three actions aligned across logging and evaluation, mark the two counterfactual rewards as unobserved, and expose the exact zero-support row. Fixed geometry makes the missing-label pattern visible without implying that missing rewards are zeros.

mediumComparison.mermaid: Rejected: a feedback-loop flowchart would show context, action, and reward, but it would not align observed and unobserved outcomes across the same action set precisely enough.
mediumComparison.svg: Selected: an original aligned action-row schematic can directly distinguish the one observed reward from two unknown counterfactuals and then show which target-policy action violates support.
mediumComparison.semanticHtml: Rejected: a table could contain the same symbols, but ordinary table reading would weaken the spatial continuity between the logged action rows and the target-policy support check.
mediumComparison.interaction: Rejected: changing propensities would add controls and state while the core identification failure is already complete in one static example.
mediumComparison.paperReuse: Rejected: the primary sources establish partial feedback, replay, propensity weighting, and doubly robust evaluation, but their figures are not needed for this narrow lesson and permissive figure-reuse rights were not established.
mediumComparison.noVisual: Rejected: the prose states that unchosen labels are missing and support is required, but readers must mentally align the logging policy, the single observed outcome, and a new policy's proposed actions.

pages.insight: The recommender-systems section divider establishes the boundary before the nearest explore/exploit discussion and contains no bandit mechanism.

The collaborative-filtering slide notes presentation-bias feedback loops and the need to trade off exploration and exploitation, but it does not define contextual actions, partial rewards, propensities, or off-policy support.
The adjacent content-based and hybrid-recommender slide moves to similarity and model blending, ending the local explore/exploit mention without adding evaluation semantics.
The ML-design overview asks about sampling biases, fresh data, online metrics, and experimentation but does not explain policy-induced missing labels.

The production checklist asks whether a model uses explore/exploit, corrects selection and position bias, and has offline and online evaluation, yet does not show logged propensities or the overlap condition.
The following project-setup slide begins a generic content-feed design sequence, marking the boundary after the production checklist.

deckReview.notes: The complete 214-page local deck was text-indexed for contextual bandit, multi-armed bandit, bandit, explore/exploit, propensity, off-policy, counterfactual, and selection bias. Only pages 130 and 162 matched the mechanism vocabulary. Their neighboring pages 129-131 and 161-163 were read to establish context and boundaries. The deck identifies exploration and bias as concerns but supplies no contextual-bandit action/reward trace, propensity-weighted evaluation, or reusable figure. No deck image, wording, coordinates, values, or layout is copied.

sources.title: A Contextual-Bandit Approach to Personalized News Article Recommendation
sources.usage: Used as a primary source to verify the sequential context-action-reward setting, adaptive learning from click feedback, and the exploration-exploitation objective.
sources.license: The paper is publicly accessible, but no permissive figure-reuse license was established. No algorithm, result, figure, prose, example values, or layout is copied.

sources.title: Unbiased Offline Evaluation of Contextual-bandit-based News Article Recommendation Algorithms
sources.usage: Used as the primary offline-evaluation source to verify that logged bandit events contain context, chosen action, and observed reward, and that evaluation can use events where the evaluated policy agrees with the logged action.
sources.license: The paper is publicly accessible, but no permissive figure-reuse license was identified. The shipped action rows and synthetic propensities are independently authored.

sources.title: Doubly Robust Policy Evaluation and Learning
sources.usage: Used as a primary source to verify that rewards are partially observed, historic action proportions may differ from a new policy, and doubly robust evaluation combines reward and logging-policy models.
sources.license: The paper is publicly accessible, but no permissive figure-reuse license was identified. No theorem, equation, data, prose, figure, or layout is reproduced.

sources.title: Bandit Algorithms
sources.usage: Used as an authoritative textbook to cross-check contextual-bandit notation, importance weighting, and the requirement that the sampling policy assign positive probability where an evaluated policy acts.
sources.license: The author-hosted Cambridge University Press book is copyrighted and no open figure license was identified. No text, proof, example, or artwork is adapted.

sourceReview.notes: The hardest prose-only mental model is selective feedback and its identification consequence. In the original synthetic event, logging policy mu assigns probabilities 0.70, 0.30, and 0 to actions A, B, and C, chooses B, and observes reward 1 only for B; the counterfactual rewards for A and C remain unknown, not zero. A target policy pi assigning probabilities 0.20, 0.30, and 0.50 has overlap for A and B but not C because pi(C|x) is positive while mu(C|x) is zero. Therefore this target policy is not identifiable from such logs without additional assumptions or new exploration. The numbers illustrate support only and make no empirical claim.

agentReview.summary: Read the complete article, searched all 214 deck pages and inspected both matching neighborhoods, then checked primary contextual-bandit, replay-evaluation, and doubly robust papers plus an authoritative bandit textbook before selecting an original aligned partial-feedback and support schematic.

implementation.accessibility: Both SVG panels have linked titles and complete descriptions. Every action, logging and target probability, observed reward, unknown counterfactual, and support verdict is directly labelled; question marks and the explicit zero-probability equation carry the lesson without color. The established two-panel primitive stacks below 640 pixels, and each 300-pixel viewBox scales without a minimum width for readability at 390 CSS pixels. Existing theme variables preserve dark-mode contrast, while shared print tokens force a light high-contrast palette and prevent page breaks inside the figure.
